key_insight: Absorbing the homogeneous operator’s inverse square root into finite element factors yields a quantum-encoded conduction operator with unit subnormalization and a condition number bounded by conductivity contrast, independent of mesh size.
engineering_relevance: The approach removes a mesh-dependent conditioning bottleneck in quantum linear solves for computational homogenization of periodic two-phase heat conduction.
method: Factor the preconditioned operator using a norm-preserving gradient and scaled diagonal conductivities.
Implement the gradient using quantum Fourier transforms and wavenumber-dependent rotations.
Use quantum singular value transformation to encode the preconditioned inverse.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests on three periodic cells with up to 10^6 unknowns confirmed mesh-independent conditioning and inverse errors below polynomial tolerance; full Qiskit state-vector simulations on 4×4 and 8×8 meshes matched finite element solutions within that tolerance.
watch_item: Full quantum-circuit validation is limited to small simulated meshes; conditioning still depends on conductivity contrast, and practical hardware advantage remains unproven.
paper_title: A Preconditioned Quantum Linear Solver for Periodic Two-Phase Heat Conduction with Mesh-Independent Condition Number
